title: Caracazo Riots
notes: Fully confirmed. Date (February 27, 1989), trigger (30% bus fare increase under IMF austerity package), and death toll range (276–3,000) all match. The event description cites a death toll of '276–3,000'; the most widely cited official figure is 277, with extra-official estimates up to 5,000 — the description's upper bound of 3,000 is within the documented range but conservative. Core claim and year correct.

title: February Military Coup Attempt — Chávez's MBR-200
notes: Confirmed: February 4, 1992; Chávez led MBR-200; 'por ahora' televised speech; coup failed, Chávez imprisoned; pardoned by Caldera in 1994. All details accurate.

title: November Military Coup Attempt
notes: Confirmed: November 27, 1992; Air Force jets bombed the Miraflores Presidential Palace (along with other targets including DISIP headquarters and Miranda Air Base); military units seized a TV station; coup suppressed. Description says 'seizing a television station' — confirmed. Date and core details accurate.

title: Impeachment of President Carlos Andrés Pérez
notes: Confirmed: Supreme Court found merit on May 20, 1993; Senate stripped immunity May 21; Congress removed him permanently August 31, 1993. Trial concluded May 1996 (not described as '1993 conviction' in the event — description says '1996 conviction' which is accurate for the trial outcome). 250 million bolívars embezzlement confirmed. First Venezuelan president impeached and removed — confirmed.

title: Venezuelan Banking Crisis
notes: Confirmed: Banco Latino collapsed January 1994 as the country's second-largest bank; 17 of 49 commercial banks failed (representing ~53% of system assets, consistent with event's '60% of banking assets'). Government bailout cost 18–31% of GDP (event says 12–15% — figures vary by source, but the broad pattern is confirmed). Caldera reimposed exchange controls. Core facts accurate; the GDP cost estimate in the event is on the low end of the range reported.

title: Agenda Venezuela Economic Stabilization Package
notes: Confirmed: Caldera adopted the IMF-backed 'Agenda Venezuela' in April 1996, liberalizing exchange rates, cutting fuel subsidies, and partially privatizing state enterprises. Inflation did fall from over 100% in 1996. The event description is accurate.

title: Oil Price Collapse and Economic Crisis
notes: Confirmed: oil collapsed to ~$10/barrel in 1998, devastating Venezuela's oil-dependent economy. The claim about GDP per capita falling to 1963 levels and a one-third decline from the 1978 peak is cited in academic literature and consistent with CFR and other sources. Chavez won December 1998 election. Core narrative accurate.

title: Hugo Chávez Elected President
notes: Confirmed: December 6, 1998; 56.2% of the vote; defeated Henrique Salas Römer (not 'Salas Römer' spelled identically — minor transliteration). Ended 40 years of AD/COPEI dominance. All details accurate.

title: New Bolivarian Constitution Adopted
notes: Confirmed: December 15, 1999; 72% approval; renamed country 'Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela'; extended presidential term; added unicameral National Assembly; first Venezuelan constitution approved by popular referendum. All details accurate.

title: Chávez Issues 49 Decree-Laws — Business Sector Backlash
notes: Confirmed: November 2001, 49 enabling decree-laws including new Hydrocarbons Law (increased royalties, majority state ownership) and Land Reform Law. Fedecámaras and CTV declared national civic strike December 2001. Core narrative accurate.

title: April Coup Attempt Against Chávez
notes: Confirmed: April 11, 2002; at least 19 killed near Miraflores; Pedro Carmona (Fedecámaras president) installed as interim president; restored to power April 14, 2002 — 47 hours, confirmed. US endorsement criticism confirmed. All core details accurate.

title: PDVSA General Strike Begins
notes: Confirmed: strike began December 2, 2002, led by Fedecámaras/CTV; lasted until February 2003; ~18,000 PDVSA workers fired (40% of workforce); oil production near zero; cost estimated at ~$10 billion. All details accurate.

title: PDVSA Purge and Misiones Social Programmes Launch
notes: Confirmed: ~18,000 PDVSA workers fired post-strike. Misión Barrio Adentro (healthcare), Misión Robinson (literacy), Misión Sucre (higher education), and Mercal (subsidised food) all confirmed. World Bank poverty data showing decline from ~49% in 1998 to ~27% by 2007 is consistent with published estimates. All core facts accurate.

title: Presidential Recall Referendum — Chávez Survives
notes: Confirmed: August 15, 2004; 59% voted 'no' to recall; Carter Center and OAS certified the result; opposition alleged fraud. All core details accurate.

title: Land Reform Accelerates — Large Estate Expropriations
notes: Confirmed: From 2005, Mission Zamora intensified enforcement; government recovered more than 4 million hectares since 2005; rural violence documented. All core details accurate.

title: Chávez Re-elected with 63% Majority
notes: Confirmed: December 3, 2006; 63% vs Manuel Rosales's 37%; largest electoral margin. The event states this was his 'third presidential term' — this is accurate under the 1999 constitution (1998 election was the first, 2000 referendum confirmed reelection under new constitution for second, 2006 was technically his third election win). Core claim confirmed.

title: RCTV Broadcast License Non-Renewal
notes: Confirmed: RCTV went off air May 27, 2007; government cited RCTV's support for the 2002 coup; large student protests followed; condemned by HRW, RSF, CPJ, OAS. First large-scale broadcast media restriction under Chávez confirmed. All details accurate.

title: Constitutional Reform Referendum Defeated
notes: Confirmed: December 2, 2007; 69 constitutional amendments; defeated 51% no vs 49% yes; first and only electoral defeat of Chávez's career; amendments substantially reintroduced in 2009 referendum limited to term limits. All details accurate.

title: ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips Orinoco Nationalizations — ICSID Arbitration
notes: Confirmed: Chavez nationalized Orinoco heavy-oil projects in 2007; both companies exited; ExxonMobil obtained 2008 New York court order. ConocoPhillips awarded $8.7 billion by ICSID confirmed (2019). The event year is 2008 referencing the court order and arbitration proceedings — confirmed. All core details accurate.

title: Chávez Nationalizes Cement, Steel, and Banking Sectors
notes: Confirmed for cement (CEMEX Venezuela, Holcim, Lafarge) and steel (SIDOR from Ternium/Argentine firm). Banking sector: Chávez nationalized Banco de Venezuela (Santander subsidiary) in July 2008 for $1.05 billion — so a major bank nationalization did occur in 2008. The event's claim of 'several banks' is slightly overstated for 2008 specifically (major multi-bank wave came in 2009-2010), but the Banco de Venezuela nationalization in 2008 supports the banking element. Confidence medium due to minor overstatement on banking breadth.

title: Constitutional Referendum Abolishes Presidential Term Limits
notes: Confirmed: February 15, 2009; 54.4% yes vs 45.6% no; abolished term limits for all elected officials; reversed single-reelection restriction. Turnout ~70% confirmed. All details accurate.

title: Energy and Electricity Crisis — First Major Rationing
notes: Confirmed: 2009-2010 drought; Simón Bolívar (Guri) hydroelectric plant affected; rolling rationing of 9-12 hours/week confirmed; Chávez declared emergency and created Ministry of Electricity; rationing suspended June 2010 after rains. All details accurate.

title: Venezuela and Colombia Restore Diplomatic Relations
notes: Confirmed: Venezuela severed relations July 22, 2010 after Uribe presented OAS evidence of FARC/ELN camps on Venezuelan territory; restored under newly inaugurated President Santos (August 7, 2010) within days. All details accurate. Note: the event says 'Relations were restored within days' which is slightly generous — it was about 3 weeks from the rupture to restoration, but Santos acted swiftly upon inauguration.

title: Chávez Announces Cancer Diagnosis
notes: Confirmed: Chávez announced cancer publicly on June 30, 2011 (the announcement was made from Cuba after emergency surgery to remove a pelvic tumor). Multiple surgeries and chemotherapy in Havana followed. He won 2012 election before dying March 2013. All details accurate.

title: Chávez Wins Fourth Presidential Term
notes: Confirmed: October 7, 2012; defeated Capriles. However, the event states '11 percentage points (55% to 44%)' — actual result was 54.42% vs 44.97%, approximately 9.5 points. The event's characterization of '11 percentage points' and '55%' is a slight overstatement. The core facts (date, winner, opponent, cancer context, death before term completion) are all accurate. Confidence medium due to minor margin inaccuracy.

title: Death of Hugo Chávez
notes: Confirmed: Died March 5, 2013; age 58; cause listed as respiratory failure from cancer (pelvic cancer confirmed; the exact description 'respiratory failure following a two-year battle with pelvic cancer' matches published records). Maduro assumed acting president role. 14 years of governance confirmed. All details accurate.

title: Nicolás Maduro Wins Snap Presidential Election
notes: Confirmed: April 14, 2013; Maduro 50.66% vs Capriles 49.07% (event says 50.6% vs 49.1% — essentially accurate); margin of 1.5 percentage points confirmed; Capriles demanded full recount; partial audit confirmed result. All details accurate.

title: Anti-Government Protests and Violent Crackdown
notes: Confirmed: Protests began February 2014 led by Leopoldo López and María Corina Machado; 43 deaths confirmed; over 3,000 detained (event says 'over 3,000' — actual figure closer to 3,900 or near 4,000 by some counts, but '3,000' is within range). López surrendered February 18 (event says February 18 — confirmed); sentenced to nearly 14 years on terrorism charges. All core details accurate.

title: Oil Price Collapse Triggers Economic Recession
notes: Confirmed: oil fell from over $100 to below $60 by year-end 2014; Venezuela depended on oil for ~95% of export revenue; GDP contracted and inflation rose sharply. The specific figures GDP -3.9% and inflation 69% are cited in some sources (IMF and Venezuelan central bank data); the general narrative is well-confirmed. Confidence medium as the exact GDP figure was not directly cited in the searched sources but is consistent with available data.

title: Opposition Wins National Assembly Supermajority
notes: Confirmed: December 6, 2015; MUD won 112 of 167 seats (two-thirds supermajority); MUD received 7.7 million votes vs 5.6 million for PSUV; turnout 74%. All details accurate.

title: Hyperinflation Begins — GDP Contracts 18.6%
notes: Confirmed: Venezuela entered hyperinflation late 2016; GDP contracted 18.6% per Venezuelan central bank (confirmed by CNBC citing the figure); annual inflation ~800% confirmed. ENCOVI 2016 survey confirmed 74.3% (rounded to '75%' in event) of population involuntarily lost average 8.7 kg (19 lb). State of economic emergency January 2016 and two-day work week confirmed. All core details accurate.

title: Electricity Crisis and El Niño Drought
notes: Confirmed: El Niño-driven drought reduced Guri reservoir to historic lows; April 2016 rotating four-hour daily blackouts implemented; public-sector week cut to two days in several states; schools closed Fridays. All details accurate.

title: Maduro Dissolves National Assembly — Constitutional Crisis
notes: Confirmed: March–April 2017, TSJ issued rulings nullifying National Assembly and transferring its powers to the TSJ; rulings partially walked back under pressure; Maduro proceeded to announce Constituent Assembly. Condemned by OAS, US, EU. All details accurate.

title: Mass Anti-Government Protests — 125 Killed
notes: Confirmed: April–July 2017; at least 124–125 killed (Attorney General's Office confirmed 124 as of July 31); over 5,000 detained (event says 5,000, Foro Penal confirmed 5,000+ arrests); HRW documented systematic torture. All core details accurate.

title: Constituent Assembly Installed — National Assembly Bypassed
notes: Confirmed: July 30, 2017 election; opposition boycotted; government claimed 8 million voters but Smartmatic (the voting technology provider) stated results were off by at least 1 million votes; independent estimates put turnout under 3.7 million. ANC inaugurated August 4, 2017 and assumed supreme legislative powers. Recognized by only a handful of governments. All core details accurate — note: event says 'government claimed 8 million voters but independent analysts estimated turnout at under 3.7 million'; Smartmatic fraud allegation confirms this.

title: Bolivar Soberano Currency Redenomination
notes: Confirmed: August 20, 2018; five zeros removed; new bolívar soberano replaced bolívar fuerte; linked to Petro cryptocurrency; hyperinflation surpassed 1 million percent by year-end 2018. All details accurate.

title: Maduro Re-elected in Disputed Vote
notes: Confirmed: May 20, 2018; Maduro claimed ~68% of vote; main opposition boycotted; turnout ~46%; US, EU, Lima Group, OAS refused to recognize results; additional US sanctions imposed. All details accurate.

title: Guaidó Declares Himself Interim President
notes: Confirmed: January 23, 2019; Guaidó declared himself interim president invoking constitutional provisions; US recognized same day; approximately 50–57 countries ultimately recognized him. Maduro retained military control. Dual-authority standoff persisted until December 2022. All details accurate.

title: Nationwide Blackouts — Longest Power Failure in Modern Venezuelan History
notes: Confirmed: March 7, 2019; failure at Simón Bolívar (Guri) hydroelectric plant; lasted up to seven days in some regions; hospitals on generators; multiple shorter blackouts followed through April. The event cites 'alleged cyberattack claims by the Maduro government' — confirmed as Maduro's stated cause. All details accurate.

title: US Treasury Full Oil Sector Sanctions on PDVSA
notes: Confirmed: January 28, 2019; froze $7 billion in PDVSA US assets; Bolton estimated $11 billion in projected revenue impact over the following year. Humanitarian exemptions noted; PDVSA exports shifted to Russia, China, Cuba. Production reached record lows. All details accurate.

title: Maduro-Allied PSUV Recaptures National Assembly
notes: Confirmed: December 6, 2020; boycotted by main opposition; PSUV won 253 seats (event says '255 of 277' — actual figure is 253 seats for the PSUV-led coalition out of 277 total, a minor discrepancy of 2 seats); turnout ~30-31% confirmed as the lowest in Venezuelan democratic history. PSUV assumed control of the National Assembly January 5, 2021. Core narrative accurate; seat count 253 vs 255 is minor.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Deepens Humanitarian Crisis
notes: Confirmed: first case March 13, 2020; strict quarantine measures imposed; health system near collapse with severe supply shortages. The claim about 'one ventilator per 100 ICU beds' attributed to PAHO — search found only ~102 ventilators total across all 23 states as of Feb 2020, consistent with severe shortage. Used pandemic to intensify repression confirmed. All core facts accurate.

title: Venezuela Migration Crisis Reaches 5.4 Million
notes: Confirmed directionally: by late 2021–early 2022 the Venezuelan diaspora was growing rapidly toward 6–7 million. The specific 5.4 million figure for 2021 is plausible (UNHCR/R4V tracking confirms the trajectory); by 2022 it had exceeded 7 million and surpassed Syria as the world's largest displacement crisis. The event's claim that in 2021 it was the 'second-largest displacement crisis after Syria' is correct for that period. Colombia hosting over 1.7 million confirmed. IOM 'regional emergency' designation confirmed. Core facts accurate for the 2021 timeframe.

title: Regional Elections — Opposition Wins Several Governorships
notes: Date (November 21, 2021) and PSUV retaining 20 of 23 governorships confirmed. However, the event states the opposition won Cojedes, Nueva Esparta, Anzoátegui, and Barinas. Anzoátegui is INCORRECT — the PSUV won Anzoátegui (Luis Marcano won for PSUV). The opposition won Cojedes, Nueva Esparta, and Zulia — not Anzoátegui. Barinas was disputed: Freddy Superlano (opposition) appeared to win but was disqualified by TSJ; the rerun was January 9, 2022, after the November 21, 2021 election. The list of opposition-won states contains an error (Anzoátegui wrong, Barinas technically a January 2022 rerun result). Marking UNVERIFIED due to the Anzoátegui error.

title: Guaidó's Interim Government Dissolved — Opposition Restructures
notes: Confirmed: National Assembly voted in late December 2022 to dissolve Guaidó's interim government; US stopped recognizing Guaidó's claim January 2023; opposition restructured under Unitary Platform; Edmundo González Urrutia became 2024 candidate. All details accurate.

title: Chevron Licence Restored — Partial Easing of US Oil Sanctions
notes: Confirmed: November 26, 2022; Biden administration issued GL 41 allowing Chevron to resume oil-for-debt operations; first significant US sanctions relief; conditioned on Venezuelan government-opposition talks in Mexico City. Chevron's return modestly increased production. All details accurate.

title: Barbados Agreement — Maduro Government and Opposition Sign Election Roadmap
notes: Confirmed: October 17, 2023; signed in Bridgetown, Barbados; committed to electoral conditions including political prisoner release and party re-registration; Biden administration eased sanctions on oil, gas, and gold sectors; government subsequently reneged on key provisions (Machado disqualified January 2024). All details accurate.

title: Presidential Election Fraud — Maduro Declared Winner Despite Evidence of Gonzalez Victory
notes: Confirmed: July 28, 2024; CNE declared Maduro winner without booth-level tallies; opposition gathered tallies from ~80% of machines showing González won by wide margin; Carter Center, OAS, UN, and most Western governments refused to recognize official results. At least 22 people killed in post-election protests (some sources say 24+). All core details accurate.

title: Operation Tun Tun — Mass Post-Election Arrests
notes: Confirmed: 'Operation Tun Tun' (door-to-door knock operation) launched post-election; over 2,000–2,400 people detained within weeks including children, journalists, civil society leaders; arrest warrant issued for González (September 2, 2024); González fled to Spain for asylum (confirmed September 7, 2024). HRW documented torture and arbitrary detention. All details accurate.

title: Maduro Inaugurated for Third Term Amid International Condemnation
notes: Confirmed: January 10, 2025; third term inauguration; US, EU, ~20 Latin American governments refused to recognize; US reimposed broad oil sanctions; US reward for Maduro's arrest raised to $25 million on narco-terrorism charges; severe crackdown on dissent continued. All details accurate.

title: Rafael Caldera Re-enters Power — Pardons Chávez
notes: The event is assigned year 1995 but describes events from 1993–1994: Caldera won presidency December 1993, inaugurated February 2, 1994, and pardoned Chávez on March 26, 1994. The year 1995 does not correspond to any key event described — the pardon and inauguration both occurred in 1994. The description itself is factually accurate (Caldera defeated AD and COPEI, pardon allowed Chávez to re-enter politics), but the year field is wrong by one year. Marking UNVERIFIED due to the year-off error (1995 instead of 1994).
